governance.scopeChange: Do not add mandatory items, raise targets, or split/reweight items during execution without explicit user approval. Record proposals in deferredBacklog. A defect that prevents an existing criterion is fixed within that item, not new scope.
governance.noSpeculativeHardening: Tie every implementation/hardening change to a failing criterion, missing required evidence, or a reproducible defect under a checklist ID. Stop improving a satisfied criterion.
governance.unknownFirst: Before building a not_audited item, inspect and qualify existing code; reuse Books, Documents, Signing and mobile work. Complete baseline qualification before interpreting percentages as a total completion estimate.
governance.workUnit: At turn start name checklist IDs and the evidence needed. At turn end update status, evidence and the next concrete action. A log entry without item progress is not completion.
governance.evidence: No full-workflow credit for source checks, mocked service tests or single-session SQL fixtures. Real provider, full-schema, concurrency, browser and measured performance requirements remain separate.
governance.verificationFreshness: Record source hashes and environment for proof. Changed evidence dependencies invalidate that proof until reassessed. Existing live environment is production; no customer test mutations.
governance.blocking: External gates never silently disappear or count as complete. Report implementation complete awaiting external acceptance when only these remain; do not keep generating features.
governance.regressions: Preserve existing residential/commercial and mixed-org behavior. Use agreed regression checks; repeated broad tests require a code change, failure or unresolved concern.
governance.finish: When all mandatory items are accepted and no launch blocker remains, complete the goal and move optional enhancements to a separate backlog.

statusDefinitions.not_audited: Existing capability not sufficiently assessed; neither missing nor implemented credit.
statusDefinitions.pending: Known unmet criterion or required new acceptance task.
statusDefinitions.partial: Some relevant implementation exists; at least one criterion remains incomplete or unqualified.
statusDefinitions.implemented: Every functional criterion has code or the required engineering artifact; required integration/QA proof or release gates still remain.
statusDefinitions.verified: Every verificationRequired tier has fresh successful evidence against every criterion.
statusDefinitions.accepted: Verified, deployment/activation is complete or explicitly not applicable, all release dependencies are accepted, and the release owner records acceptance.

progressRules.implementation: Sum frozen weights for implemented, verified or accepted / all mandatory weights. No fractional credit for partial.
progressRules.verification: Sum weights for verified or accepted / all mandatory weights.
progressRules.releaseReady: Sum weights for accepted / all mandatory weights.
progressRules.automationCoverage: Separate count of items with passing isolated automated evidence. This is not verified/readiness progress.
progressRules.weights: Fixed relative complexity estimates: 1 narrow capability, 2 workflow, 3 transactional/multi-system/operational requirement. These are not remaining-time estimates.
progressRules.uncertainty: Until not_audited items are qualified, implementation percentage is a documented lower bound, not a project ETA or replacement for the earlier rough 30% estimate.

proposedScope.reason: Every closing hands off to warranty, and editable coverage terms are a data-integrity gap.

criteriaVerdicts.evidence: Publication is ordered and checked: assertReleaseCompletion plus assertReleaseGateCompletion, then a CAS update to 'released' on the lease token (starts-pipeline.ts:404-416). The event uses an idempotencyId and notifications use idempotency ids (starts-pipeline.ts:225-243). confirmation recovery exists behind a flag (lib/services/starts-confirmation-recovery.ts, 20261003045000). These are still separate commits: the finalize step writes lot/project separately (380-388), the status update, recordEvent and notifyAssignedSuper are separate, and no recordAudit is emitted for release publication in the worker.

cancelRelease (starts.ts:862-892) sets the package to 'ready' with no lease token check and resets steps/outbox in a non-atomic Promise.all. The worker detects the change only at its next assertReleaseLease, so an in-flight artifact write between checks can land after the cancel (TOCTOU). The staged fences would close this but are not consumed. retryRelease (827-850) blindly overwrites the status and lease without CAS on 'attention'.

deferredBacklog.proposal: No checklist item covers division-aware database enforcement: division isolation is app-layer only and services often use the user client where RLS is org-only. Propose an item for division RLS/RPC backstops, or fold it into EP02-04 with approval.
Region level appears only in EP02-01. If no customer needs it, propose an explicit exclusion.

Lot status conflates sales state ('assigned') with land delivery ('developed'); EP04-04 cannot be met while reservation advances an undeveloped lot to 'assigned'. Propose a separate delivery/readiness fact on lots (or phase) — may need explicit scope decision.

No checklist item covers removing the legacy (non-atomic) writers once atomic catalog publication, agreement creation and reservation conversion are activated (migration headers say 'legacy writer cutover remain required'); propose a cutover/deletion item or fold it into EP03-04/EP04-06 remainingWork explicitly.

Lot-fit (EP03-06), acquisition diligence (EP04-01) and entitlements (EP04-02) are greenfield domains; propose they be explicitly sized as new-entity work (schema + RBAC + search + events) rather than audit items.

Scope conflict to resolve: docs/production-expansion/06-sales-contracts-closings.md:70-84 and :970 explicitly placed lead ingestion/OSC, commissions, escrow/title integrations and lender status tracking OUT of scope, yet EP05-01, EP05-05 and EP05-06 are mandatory. Owner should either confirm the build or move them to deferredBacklog.

Selection lock at purchase agreement execution (lib/services/community-sales.ts:1522) locks every selection, not only structural ones; if unintended it breaks the post-contract design studio flow (EP06-01/02/03) - propose verifying under EP06-03 rather than new scope.

Interactive starts mutations (open/update/attest/waive/reopen/refresh/release/retry/cancel/notice-retry) should move to authorized service-side RPCs. This is needed for the staged fences to be appliable at all. It partly fits EP07-11/13, but the interactive-path rewrite is not named by any criterion.
Starts readiness depends on a permit record, and no permit entity exists. The scorecard's E06-03 'Complete permit lifecycle' should own a permit record that the EP07-01 gate can auto-derive from.

Price-book mutation authorization by parent scope (create/reprice/void/end agreements for division-restricted buyers) is not explicitly owned by any EP08 criterion; propose folding into EP08-03 or EP02 least-privilege.

Punch create/update authorization (no permission/project check in app/(app)/projects/[id]/actions.ts) is a cross-cutting least-privilege defect larger than EP09-05; propose an EP02 launch-blocking defect entry.
Mobile per-module requireProject duplication (8 copies in lib/mobile/*, one org-only) — propose one shared mobile project authorization helper under EP09-01/EP02 to prevent future drift.

Warranty scheduling timezone/DST: dispatch desk renders visit windows in UTC (app/(app)/warranty/warranty-desk-client.tsx:301,310) and appointment/dispatch emails format with server-local toLocaleString (lib/services/warranty-operations.ts:745,763). Scorecard E11-02 requires DST-correct calendars but no checklist criterion covers it; propose adding it to EP11-04 acceptance.

Warranty coverage DB immutability (project_warranty_coverage writable by any authenticated org member) is not an explicit criterion; propose a hardening sub-criterion under EP11-02 rather than new scope.

Data export/offboarding and document continuity (scorecard E12-03: archive/export/restore and document continuity) has no EP12 checklist item; only Books restore tooling partially touches it. Propose an item or explicitly map E12-03 to EP13-08 + EP12-04.

Production-targeting safety preflight for all acceptance/benchmark scripts (scorecard F02 DoD) is not a checklist item; scripts/benchmark-project-directory.mjs reads production with the service role key. Propose a narrow item (or fold into EP13-01 criteria via scope control).
Plan finish-line gate 'every production-visible page/action/job is covered; no orphan surfaces' (F01) has no checklist item; surfaceInventory is metadata, not an acceptance item.
Scenario A12 (multi-entity/division/mixed-posture operating month and close) has no EP14 acceptance item; propose mapping to an EP10/EP14 item.

Synchronous import commit of up to 10,000 Open-WIP rows inside a server action will exceed function time limits at enterprise scale; covered by EP12-03 remediation (async durable job) — no new item needed, flagged for priority.

proposal.scopeReason: Setting trade prices by community and plan is the core of how a production builder buys, so it must work on day one.
Buyers at a 25–250 closing builder work these lists daily, and division scoping is an access rule.
It is an access-control gap, and mixed or multi-division orgs are the design case.
It ships on the bid page buyers use from day one and only needs a small fix and checking.
A cancelled award that keeps pricing purchase orders is a money-integrity defect, and yearly price renewals are routine for production builders.
Cutting POs per home is the daily purchasing job and the gaps touch what gets ordered.
Duplicate purchase orders are a money-integrity risk.
Showing vendors unissued draft orders is an exposure defect, and order confirmation is expected by production trades.
Approval controls and separation of duties on money are security and money-integrity gaps.
A first 25–250-closing builder can log deliveries in daily reports and handle shortages with variance POs; structured delivery tracking is a scale feature.
Paying trades against approved obligations is money integrity for every closing.
Variance tracking is how a production builder controls margin from the first community.
This is an authorization gap on money-touching field actions.
Supers on raw lots routinely lose signal, and silent overwrites corrupt the field record.
Building the wrong option or off a superseded plan is the core field-quality risk for production homes.
Inspection failures gating closing is a core production quality control.
Missing authorization and a closing gate that can be bypassed are security and close-integrity gaps.
A super running 10–20 homes needs the cross-home view, and misfiled evidence is a record-integrity issue.
Punch dispatch plus the trade portal covers a first production builder; PO-linked threads and supplier messaging are refinements.
The workflows and speed targets are best set and proven with a real builder's supers on their devices.
Production builders routinely hold land in a separate company, and the intercompany and per-company tie-outs are money integrity.
Mis-keyed land purchases and redated starts happen in the first months, and without a correction path the books get stuck.
A production builder's cash is driven by starts, closings and takedowns, and the current report both leaks other divisions' numbers and undercounts silently.
House margin is a headline number for a production builder and a wrong one undermines trust immediately.
At 25-250 closings a year the 1,000-row cut-off is hit almost immediately, so the report is wrong for the first customer.
Whether and how the first builder finances houses (per-house construction loans vs a revolving line) must come from that customer and lender before this is built.
Needs the first customer's chosen accounting system and a sandbox of it to prove parity.
The close gate is the builder's guarantee that the books are right each month.

A 25-250-closing builder starts with several years of homes in warranty, and the warranty desk is useless for them until they are imported; the code can be built now and rehearsed with the customer's file.
It is an authorization gap on a customer-facing obligation, and those are always fixed before the first builder.
Honest on-time reporting is the core of a warranty desk and the fix is small; automatic routing can follow but the breach bug cannot.
Homeowners not being told about moved or cancelled appointments is a day-one customer-care failure for a warranty team.
Without a reject path, bad repairs get closed as resolved and the warranty cost is booked against unaccepted work.
Duplicate vendor credits are a money-integrity defect.
Warranty reserve accounting is money integrity on every home closed.
Trend feedback becomes valuable after a year of warranty history; a first builder can run warranty without the review workflow, though deploying the analytics is cheap.

scenarios.story: A presold home from lot takedown to warranty: lot released, buyer reserves, agreement signed with deposit, selections by cutoff, permit, start released, POs issued, built, closed, enrolled in warranty, and the books tie (land basis, inventory, deposit, revenue, reserve).
scenarios.existingSupport: HOME-01 (land allocation→sale at cost→deposit→warranty reserve→reversed closing), tests/support/starts-harness.js, agreement/esign PGlite suites
scenarios.result: core passing; re-run pending after fixes

scenarios.story: Reservation to signed purchase agreement: lot hold, incentive within capacity, catalog revision locked, buyer signs, deposit received and applied only to that home.
scenarios.existingSupport: agreement-creation-db, reservation-conversion-db, agreement-incentive-capacity-db suites; BILL-01 deposit handling

scenarios.story: Selections and cutoffs: buyer picks options from the published catalog, a late change after cutoff becomes a priced change order/VPO, and option balances reconcile.
scenarios.existingSupport: configuration-rules-db, selection-variance-orders, catalog publication suites (PGlite only)

scenarios.story: Start release: gates checked, release creates schedule and POs exactly once, a crashed or retried release does not duplicate, and a stale-role or other-division user is refused.
Spec home: started without a buyer, ages in inventory (and is written down if needed), converts to a buyer without rewriting released costs or plan version, final margin ties.
scenarios.existingSupport: HOME-01, LOSS-01 (home write-down), MIG-01 spec openings, spec-inventory-aging tests

scenarios.story: Cancellation before and after release: deposit refunded or forfeited, reservation released, trades and POs cancelled, lot back to inventory; an interrupted cancel retried yields one outcome.
scenarios.existingSupport: RACE-01 pattern and HOME-01 reversal only

scenarios.story: A permit or supply delay shifts dependent schedules, start capacity and promised-close risk; an approved schedule change updates obligations consistently.
An imported pre-Arc home and a newly closed home go through warranty request, dispatch, offline phone visit, verification, dispute and trade backcharge; coverage and reserve tie.
scenarios.existingSupport: HOME-01 warranty reserve consumption, mobile-warranty-visits, warranty-completion-transaction-db; installed-home import missing

scenarios.story: A production builder comes over: communities, lots, plans, open homes with buyers, agreements, budgets and POs, deposits, installed homes and Books openings; counts reconcile to source and a crash mid-file resumes.
scenarios.existingSupport: MIG-01 (Books openings incl. land and spec homes), tests/imports-open-wip.test.js (fake client)

scenarios.story: Who can do what across production desks: sales consultant, purchasing, starts manager, superintendent, warranty tech, division-scoped manager and another org's member try every production path; every refusal is server-side.
scenarios.existingSupport: AUTH-01 pattern, app-sweep (owner only), authorization suites

scenarios.story: Production money under contention: two sessions sign the same lot, double-release a start, approve the same VPO, cancel during release; outcomes are serial-equivalent or refused and cents conserve.

First-builder volume: 2 divisions, 12 communities, 1,000 lots, 250 active homes, 2,500 warranty homes, a year of history; desks and phone stay within p95 targets with 50 concurrent users and totals stay correct.
scenarios.existingSupport: CAP-01 request/row meter, isolated stack, upgrade-seed

scenarios.story: Every production role (owner, sales, land, starts, purchasing, design studio, superintendent, warranty) signs in and opens the production desks and a home's workbench tabs at desktop width: its own desk opens clean, anything else is a named permission refusal, never a crash, console error or 5xx.

Operators find homes, lots, plans, buyers, projects and vendors by typing: Find-a-home searches, filters by price, beds and availability, sorts and pages on the server with one asking price for every viewer; a returning buyer is found and attached instead of duplicated; a division-limited member never sees another division; a page past the end is empty; no step needs an id.

Divisions, roles and security: a member limited to one division sees none of another division's homes, communities, lots, search results or tasks, and another builder reaches nothing; moving a community carries its lots and homes in one step and keeps their division history; a limited member cannot move a community out of reach; an inviter cannot hand out more than they hold; suspending someone revokes their sessions and cancels their queued work; whoever enters a bill cannot approve it and the refusal is audited; a lost audit record is never a clean success and is written later under the same correlation id; Arc staff reach a builder only through a stated, time-limited grant the owner can see (browser journey).

Required two-factor: an owner turns it on and is held to it at once; a member without a factor is sent to set it up and the API refuses them; a wrong code is refused at sign-in and a password-only session cannot open the app; an admin reset ends the member's sessions and sends them back to setup; turning it off frees new sessions. Runs in its own organization on the acceptance stack (journeys/required-mfa.spec.ts).

Product and configuration: a sold home keeps the revisions it was priced and released at; a selection group confirms all or nothing; a stale catalog refuses a selection write under a real concurrent publication; plan offerings and lot fit hold everywhere with evidenced overrides; production pricing never guesses; a signed price and the original margin cannot be rewritten; a plan change reaches each sold home only by an authorized decision; an invalid configuration explains itself with fixes that respect locks.

verificationRule.rule: An item is verified when every golden scenario it maps to (scenarioIds) passed on the isolated acceptance stack with current evidence, and its source review is current. Same rule as the Arc Books readiness tracker. Per-criterion tests remain as regression protection, not a gate; race proof comes from race scenarios.
verificationRule.replaces: Per-item verificationRequired tiers with explicit coverage of every criterion.
